en: The Sūtra on Receiving the New Year Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi Nation during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Eastern Garden, the Deer Mother’s Park, in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, together with...
There was a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the World-Honored One sat upon a seat spread out in the open air, surrounded before and behind by the community of bhikṣus.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Go now to the open space and quickly strike the *gandī*.
Why is this? Today, the fifteenth day of the seventh month, is the day for receiving the new year."
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and spoke this verse:
“Your pure eyes have no equal; There is nothing you have not mastered.
Your wisdom is free from defilement and attachment— What is it called to observe the *varṣā*?”
At that time, the World-Honored One again spoke these verses in response to Ānanda:
"When the three karmas of the annual retreat are purified— whatever has been done by body,
speech, and mind— two bhikṣus face one another, each confessing their own transgressions."
He then announced his own name: "Today the assembly observes the *poṣadha*;
I too shall observe it with a pure mind. I only pray that you will forgive my transgressions.
At that time, Ānanda again asked concerning the ritual procedure with this verse:
"Are all the Buddhas of the past, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, as well as the Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas,
possessed of these same Buddha-dharmas?
Or are they unique to Śākyamuni alone?"
At that time, the World-Honored One further replied to Ānanda in verse:
"The disciples with pure minds Of the Buddhas of the past, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, Possess all these Buddha-dharmas; It is not unique to Śākyamuni alone."
Pratyekabuddhas do not possess this Dharma; they have no rainy-season retreat and no disciples.
They travel alone without companions and do not preach the Dharma to others.
As for the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who will appear in the future, they are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and beyond calculation.
“They too shall observe this year-long retreat, just as in the Dharma of the present Gautama.

At that time, having heard these words, the Venerable Ānanda was filled with such joy and exultation that he could not contain himself; he immediately ascended the lecture hall, took up the *gandī* mallet, and spoke thus:
“I now strike this drum of the Tathāgata’s faith; let all those who are disciples of the Tathāgata assemble here in full.”
At that time, Ānanda spoke these verses again:
"Having subdued the enemy of Māra’s power, And eliminated the fetters without remainder, He strikes the ghaṇṭā in the open air; May the bhikṣus hear it and assemble."
"All you who wish to hear the Dharma, To cross the flood of the ocean of birth and death,
Having heard this wondrous sound, All should gather here with haste.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having struck the ghaṇṭā, approached the World-Honored One, prostrated himself at his feet, stood to one side, and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"Now is precisely the right time; we only pray that the World-Honored One will command us!
What task do you wish for us to perform?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Sit down in order; the Tathāgata himself shall know the proper time.
At that time, the World-Honored One sat upon the grass seat and addressed the bhikṣus:
"All of you should sit upon grass seats as well."
The bhikṣus replied, “So be it,
World-Honored One! Thereupon,
the bhikṣus each sat down upon grass mats.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having silently observed the bhikṣus, addressed them:
“I now wish to observe the New Year; am I free from fault regarding the assembly?”
"And have you not transgressed in body, speech, or mind?
After the Tathāgata had spoken these words, the bhikṣus remained silent and did not respond.
At that time, the Tathāgata again addressed the bhikṣus three times:
"I now wish to observe the New Year; however, am I free from faults regarding the assembly?
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra rose from his seat, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"The assembly of bhikṣus observes the Tathāgata and finds no fault in his body, speech, or mind."

The reason for this is that today the World-Honored One delivers those not yet delivered, liberates those not yet liberated, and enables those who have not attained nirvana to attain it. He provides protection for those without protection, serves as eyes for the blind, and acts as the King of Physicians for the sick. Solely honored within the three realms, there is none who can equal him; he is the most venerable and supreme.

He causes those who have not yet resolved to attain the Way to generate that resolve; he leads those among the multitude who have not yet awakened to awakening; he enables those who have not heard the Dharma to hear it; and for those who are lost, he creates a path and guides them with the True Dharma.
"By reason of these matters, the Tathāgata is without fault toward the assembly, nor does he have any transgression of body, speech, or mind.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I now likewise declare myself before the Tathāgata; am I then without fault or blame regarding the Tathāgata and the community of bhikṣus?"
The World-Honored One said:
"Now, Śāriputra, you have no non-practice whatsoever performed by body, speech, or mind."

The reason for this is that your wisdom now is such that none can equal it: it is wisdom of manifold kinds, immeasurable wisdom, boundless wisdom, wisdom without peer, swift wisdom, nimble wisdom, profound wisdom, and impartial wisdom.

In the state of joy characterized by few desires and contentment, there are many skillful means; with mindfulness undisturbed, one possesses *dhāraṇī* and *samādhi*. Fully endowed with the roots of virtue and the precepts, one achieves *samādhi*, achieves wisdom, achieves liberation, achieves the knowledge and vision of liberation, and achieves valor. One is able to endure what is taught, recognizes that evil is contrary to the Dharma, and maintains a composed and orderly mind, refraining from all rashness and violence.
Just as the eldest son of a Wheel-Turning Sage King, who is destined to succeed to the royal throne and turn the precious wheel, so too is Śāriputra;

he turns the unsurpassed, pure wheel of Dharma, which neither gods, humans, nor dragons, spirits, māras, or celestial māras have ever turned before. What you have now spoken is always in accordance with the principles of the Dharma and has never deviated from reason.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"These five hundred bhikṣus are all about to undergo the *varṣā* (rain-retreat) ceremony; do these five hundred people have no transgressions against the Tathāgata?"
The World-Honored One said:
"I do not reproach these five hundred bhikṣus for their conduct of body, speech, or mind.

Why is this? Within this assembly of Śāriputra, it is exceedingly pure and free from all blemishes; even the lowest-ranking member of this assembly has attained the stage of Srotāpanna and shall certainly eventually reach the stage of non-retrogression."
"For this reason, I do not resent or reproach this assembly.

At that time, Puṇṇa was present in the assembly; he immediately rose from his seat, went before the World-Honored One, prostrated himself at the Buddha's feet, and addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I am now capable and wish to discuss a certain matter."
The World-Honored One said,
"If you wish to say something, now is precisely the right time.
Thereupon, Puṇṇa Kassapa, before the Buddha, praised the Buddha and the community of bhikṣus, and spoke this verse:
"On the fifteenth day of purity, five hundred bhikṣus gathered;
all their fetters and knots were completely untied, and craving having ceased, it would not arise again.
Like a Great Holy Wheel-Turning King surrounded by his ministers,"
Pervading all worlds, both heavens and the human realm;
a great general who leads the masses of men, acting as a guide for humanity;
disciples joyfully attend him, and he is thoroughly possessed of the three insights and six supernormal powers.
"All are true sons of the Buddha, free from the dust and defilements;
able to sever the thorns of sensual craving, today they take refuge.
At that time, the World-Honored One approved of what Paṅgika said.
At that time, Puṇika thought to himself:
"The Tathāgata has approved what I have said.
Overjoyed and leaping for joy beyond measure, he rose from his seat, paid homage to the Buddha, and withdrew to return to his original place.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“Among my śrāvakas, the foremost disciple for composing verses is the bhikṣu Puṇṇa;
the one whose speech is free from doubt or difficulty is also the bhikṣu Puṇṇa.”
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
Regarding this *Pravāraṇā-sūtra* translated by Zhu Fahu, both the Guo and Song editions include it within the Yong case;
however, in the Danzang (Dunhuang canon), there is a work titled *Shousui jing* in the Yong case which differs greatly from this sūtra.
Now, if one examines this according to the *Kaiyuan lu*, the scripture in the Danzang (the "Cinnabar" canon) is precisely the *Shousui jing* from the Rong case.
This [scripture] in the Songzang is textually different but identical in meaning to the *Xinsui jing* in this Jing case; it appears to be the same original work translated differently.
Thus, the fact that the *Kaiyuan lu* classifies the *Xinsui jing* as a single-translation text remains its meaning obscure.
For now, wishing to categorize them together to await future sages and philosophers, I have thus moved this scripture to be included in the final volume.
